subject.title: [Feature]: Per-binding and per-agent permissionMode for ACP sessions

question: Should scoped ACP permission defaults be exposed as generic `permissionProfile` defaults on `bindings[].acp` and `agents.list[].runtime.acp`, or as ACPX-specific `permissionMode` and `nonInteractivePermissions` keys?
rationale: The missing capability is source-proven, but the durable public config shape controls write and shell authority for non-interactive channel-bound sessions and should not be chosen by repair automation.

options.title: Use Generic Permission Profiles
options.body: Add scoped `permissionProfile` defaults that map through the existing ACP runtime option alias layer, keeping ACPX-specific names at plugin-global setup unless explicitly needed.

options.title: Add ACPX-Specific Scoped Keys
options.body: Implement the requested `permissionMode` and optional `nonInteractivePermissions` precedence directly for ACPX sessions, accepting a backend-specific public config surface.

options.title: Keep Global Config Only
options.body: Document `/acp permissions` and global ACPX config as the supported paths and leave static scoped permission defaults out for now.

recommendation.title: Use Generic Permission Profiles
recommendation.body: Add scoped `permissionProfile` defaults that map through the existing ACP runtime option alias layer, keeping ACPX-specific names at plugin-global setup unless explicitly needed.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the ACP runtime option path and ACPX integration history most directly tied to the durable permission contract.
